Before The Chief Judge, Court Of Small Causes,

 *******

Chandra vs Punith Kumar on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118891447/

1 Husband, and major son of Manjula filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of Hero Honda Splendor bike bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 alleging that on 11.02.2024 at 11.00 a.m. when Manjula was traveling by sitting on the pillion of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 rode by Kiran Kumar near Bengaluru- Mangalore NH-75, towards Kothipura under bridge, Heruru service road, Kunigal taluk,
Kiran Kumar negligently rode the bike and dashed the same to the Tempo bearing No.KA-03-9222 which was running from Kothipura side towards Dombarahatti, thereby caused accident, caused instantaneous death of Manjula.

2. As on the date of accident Manjula being aged about 39 years, used to earn Rs.750/- to 800/- per day by doing coolie, agriculture and vending flowers and used to contribute the entire income to the family.
3.
Regarding accident Kunigal police registered a case in crime No.71/2024 against the rider of the bike.
4. In spite of service of the notice, the respondent No.1-owner of the motorcycle remained absent.

5. In response to the notice respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the reason and mode of accident, age, occupation and income of Manjula.

Respondent No.2-insurance company asserted that under policy issued to the motorcycle risk of own damage was covered for a period from 15.11.2022 to 14.11.2023 and risk of the liability only cover from 15.11.2022 to 14.11.2027 and risk of the pillion rider is not covered.
6.

On the basis of the pleadings on 22.10.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 11.02.2024 at about 11.00 a.m. on service road of Bengaluru- Mangalore NH-75 under Herur bridge, Kunigal Taluk, in view of the negligent use of the Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06- HP-4223 Motorcycle dashed to Goods Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-03-9222, thereby accident taken place resulting in the death of Manjula W/o Chandra, pillion rider of Motorcycle?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
7. On 20.09.2024, 22.10.2024, petitioner No.2 Arun Kumar deposed as PW1 and produced 11 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.11.
On 13.02.2025 the respondent No.2- insurance company produced the evidence of an officer as RW.1 and produced copy of the policy at Ex.R.2.

On 21.12.2024 learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 produced the copy of the policy as Ex.R.1.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

Chandra vs Punith Kumar on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118891447/
2 9.

On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.23,17,112/- with current and future interest at 6%p..a. as compensation from respondent No.1.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence PW1 Arun Kumar, son of Manjula stated that on 11.02.2024 at 11.00 a.m. when his mother Manjula was traveling by sitting on the pillion of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 rode by Kiran Kumar near Bengaluru-Mangalore NH-75, towards Kothipura under bridge, Heruru service road, Kunigal taluk, Kiran Kumar negligently rode the bike and dashed the same to the Tempo bearing No.KA-03-9222 which was running from Kothipura side towards Dombarahatti, thereby caused accident, caused instantaneous death of Manjula.
11.
In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident.
12. In the cross-examination, PW1 stated that he never witnessed the accident.
13. In the evidence RW1-officer of the insurance company/respondent No.2 stated nothing regarding reason and mode of the accident.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.71/2024 registered by Kunigal police station against Kiran Kumar-rider of Hero Honda Splendor bike bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 337, 304A of IPC, on the basis of complaint presented by Paramesh S/o Gangaiah.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the spot mahazar with photos.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of vehicle seizure mahazar with photos.
Ex . P.4
is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident
. Ex.P.5 is the copy of the Motor vehicle accident report.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of inquest mahazar.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of the PM report.

Ex.P.10 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Kunigal police in crime No.71/2024 against Kiran Kumara L.C. S/o Chandra, driver of Hero Honda Splendor bike bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279,304(A) of IPC.
In the police records name of the Manjula is noted as pillion rider of bike bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 and victim of the accident.

15. In the file there are no evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the PW.1 regarding reason,
mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 11.02.2024 at 11.00 a.m.
when Manjula was traveling by sitting on the pillion of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06- HP-4223 rode by Kiran Kumar near Bengaluru-Mangalore NH-75, towards Kothipura under bridge, Heruru service road, Kunigal taluk, Kiran Kumar negligently rode the bike and dashed the same to the Tempo bearing No.KA-03-9222 which was running from Kothipura side towards Dombarahatti,
thereby caused accident, caused instantaneous death of Manjula.

Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Chandra vs Punith Kumar on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118891447/
3 affirmative .

16. Issue No.2: In the evidence PW1 stated that as on the date of accident his mother Manjula being aged about 39 years, used to earn Rs.750/- to Rs.800/- per day by vending flowers, doing agriculture and Rs.400/- per day, by working as Coolie and used to contribute entire income to the family.
17. In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of deceased Manjula as on the date of accident.
18. In the cross-examination PW1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident his mother never earning Rs.750/- to Rs.800/- per day from Coolie work and Rs.400/- per day by vending flowers.
19. In the evidence RW.1-officer of the insurance company stated nothing regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased Manjula.
20. In the inquest mahazar and postmortem report age of deceased is noted as 44 years.
In the copy of the aadhaar card marked at Ex.P.11 date of birth of the deceased Manjula is noted as 20.06.1981.
The aadhaar cards and ration card shows that present petitioners are husband and son of Manjula.
In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of Manjula.

Hence, I have calculated the loss of dependency presuming that as on the date of accident deceased Manjula being aged 43 years, use to earn Rs.16,000/- per month by vending flowers, adding 25% income as future prospects, deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses and applying multiplier 14 in the following terms:
Approximate age of the deceased as on the 43 years date of accident - Monthly income of deceased Manjula as on - Rs.16,000/- the date of accident Add:
25% income towards future prospects Rs. 20,000/- 16000 +4000 (25%) = 20,000 Less : 1/ 3rd towards personal expenses of Rs.13,334/- the deceased Manjula (20,000 - 6,666/- = 13,334) Loss of dependency 13,334/- x12x14 Rs.22,40,112/-
21.
Hence, I award Rs.22,40,112/- towards loss of dependency.

Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.88,000/- towards consortium (44,000x2).
22. Therefore, the total compensation awarded to petitioners No.1 and 2 is at Rs.23,61,112/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents.
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1. Loss of dependency 22,40,112-00 2.
Loss of estate 16,500-00 Chandra vs Punith Kumar on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118891447/
4 3. Funeral expenses 16,500-00 4. Loss of Consortium to 88,000-00 petitioners No.1 and 2 at Rs.44,000/each
Hence I answer Issue No.2 accordingly.
23. Issue No.3:

In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company and in the evidence affidavit RW1 - officer of the insurance company asserted that under policy marked at Ex.R.1 and 2 own damage risk is covered from 15.11.2022 to 14.11.2023, the liability risk is covered from 15.11.2022 to 14.11.2027, however risk of the pillion rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 is not covered under the policy marked at Ex.R.1 and 2.
24.

In the argument learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2-insurance company by analyzing terms of the policy marked at Ex.R.1 and 2 stated that under the policy risk of the pillion rider Manjula is not covered by relying on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Madras dated 29.01.2025 passed in CMA No.2093/2023 between Pula Shanmugam and another V/s Yugender Ravellah & others.

25. The copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.1 and 2 shows that since 15.11.2022 to 14.11.2023 motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 had own damage policy coverage and since 15.11.2022 to 14.11.2027 had liability risk coverage.
26. In the policy schedule nothing has been mentioned about payment of premium cover of risk of pillion rider.

Hence in the light of the judgment cited on behalf of respondent No.2-insurance company, I have inferred that under the policy marked at Ex.R.1 and 2 risk of the pillion rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HP- 4223 namely Manjula is not covered, therefore respondent No.1- owner of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and an award is to be passed directing the respondent No.1 to pay compensation.

Hence,
I answer issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondent No.1 -owner and rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 shall pay Rs.23,61,112/- (Rupees Twenty three lakhs sixty one thousand one hundred twelve only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the owner of the Hero Honda Splendor bike bearing No.KA-06-HP-4223 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners at the ratio of 80:20.

Chandra vs Punith Kumar on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118891447/
5
After deposit compensation, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioners by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.

Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- . Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 10th day of March, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
